items.title: Microplastics in water aren’t inert and make damaging chemicals on their own

items.lede: Though plastic is usually inert, tiny pieces of it have the potential to react with one of the most pervasive molecules in the environment and in our bodies.
items.title: Microplastics React With Water, a New Study Says. That’s a Problem for Biology
